name: Southern Cheyenne camp move, Indian Territory, 1870s (draft)
description: A draft diorama of a camp move in three planes: horses in front, lodges and travois and people in the middle, a layered bluff behind. Figures are placeholder forms. Not reviewed by the Cheyenne and Arapaho Tribes; not for display.

flags.text: Display needs review by the Cheyenne and Arapaho Tribes (see research/consultation-plan.md). The whole camp is a draft until then. Not for display.
The lodge shapes, the pole angles, the door and the struck cover need checking against Cheyenne practice.
The travois sizes and the loads are approximate. Check the load and how it was packed.
The horses are placeholder silhouettes in real proportions. Breed, tack and colour are not claimed.
The people are placeholder forms in poses, with no faces, no hair and no clothing pattern. They must not stand in for real people.
The skull and vertebrae are a scene choice. They are not a particular skull.
The bluff is invented to frame the camp. It has no source.
The fire ring size is typical, and the cold ash is an assumption.
The grass tufts are decoration; their size is not measured.
The grass tuft is decoration; its size is not measured.
